statement: Let n = len(nums). A sequence ys of length n is a rearrangement of nums when len(ys)=n and, for every integer v, the number of indices i with ys[i]=v equals the number of indices i with nums[i]=v; two rearrangements are considered the same when they agree at every index. Call ys squareful when for every i with 0 <= i < n-1 the sum ys[i]+ys[i+1] is a perfect square, where an integer s is a perfect square iff there exists an integer k >= 0 with k*k = s. The function returns a result r, and r is the number of distinct squareful rearrangements of nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 12 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9. These are the problem constraints.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 12 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r satisfies 0 <= r <= n! / (product over all values v occurring in nums of c_v!), where n = len(nums) and c_v is the number of occurrences of v in nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 12 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.
nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with len(nums)=1 and 0 <= nums[0] <= 10^9.

statement: The function returns a result r determined as follows: if nums[0]=nums[1], then r=1 when 2*nums[0] is a perfect square and r=0 otherwise; if nums[0] != nums[1], then r=2 when nums[0]+nums[1] is a perfect square and r=0 otherwise.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with len(nums)=2 and, for i=0,1, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9. A perfect square means an integer s for which there exists an integer k >= 0 with k*k = s.

statement: The function returns r = 1 when 2*x is a perfect square, and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 12, and there is an integer x with 0 <= x <= 10^9 such that nums[i]=x for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums). A perfect square means an integer s for which there exists an integer k >= 0 with k*k = s.

nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 12, 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 for all i, and there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and j != i, nums[i]+nums[j] is not a perfect square, where perfect square means an integer s with some integer k >= 0 satisfying k*k = s.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r > 0 if and only if there exists a sequence ys of length len(nums) that is a rearrangement of nums (same multiset of entries) and satisfies: for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, ys[i]+ys[i+1] is a perfect square.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 12 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9. A perfect square means an integer s for which there exists an integer k >= 0 with k*k = s.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on input nums and returns r' on input nums', we have r = r'.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit integers, both satisfy 1 <= length <= 12 and all entries are between 0 and 10^9, and nums' is a rearrangement of nums, meaning len(nums')=len(nums) and for every integer v the number of occurrences of v in nums' equals the number of occurrences of v in nums.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = n! / (product over all values v occurring in nums of c_v!), where n = len(nums) and c_v is the number of occurrences of v in nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 12 and 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 for all i. For every pair of indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), nums[i]+nums[j] is a perfect square, where perfect square means an integer s with some integer k >= 0 satisfying k*k = s.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r mod 2 equals P mod 2, where P is the number of distinct squareful rearrangements ys of nums such that ys[i] = ys[len(nums)-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums); squareful means that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, ys[i]+ys[i+1] is a perfect square.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 12 and 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 for all i. A perfect square means an integer s with some integer k >= 0 satisfying k*k = s.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 12 and 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 for every i. Let G be the undirected graph on indices {0,...,len(nums)-1} with an edge between distinct i and j exactly when nums[i]+nums[j] is a perfect square, where perfect square means s=t*t for some integer t>=0. Assume G is disconnected.
